newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea military cut would feed people -- Seoul.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea military cut would feed people -- Seoul.

text.p: South Korea's National Unification Minister said on Friday that if North Korea were to cut military and propaganda spending it would be able to feed its starving people.

"The food shortage in North Korea is structural and so emergency measures alone will not solve the problem," Kwon O-kie, who is also a deputy prime minister, told an international conference in Tokyo on Asia's future.
Kwon said North Korea spends $6 billion a year on military outlays and $900 million on political propaganda.
"If a fraction of this were used for the North's basic needs, the food situation would improve and the burden on their budget would be reduced significantly," Kwon said.
"The eyes of the world are on the instability of North Korea and how it solves the food issue," Kwon said.

In Seoul on Friday, South Korea announced additional food aid to North Korea, including 50,000 tonnes of corn and 300 tonnes of powdered milk. This was in addition to a $6 million donation Seoul has made to the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP).
The WFP has appealed for $98.5 million for 200,000 tonnes of aid for North Korea, which is sliding into famine following two years of floods. The United States has pledged $25 million.

Kwon said the best way to increase South Korea's economic cooperation with the North, including food aid and direct investment, was for Pyongyang to respond positively to calls to start four-way peace talks on the Korean Peninsula.
"By starting the four-way talks, we can implement a variety of economic measures, and this includes proposed direct investment," Kwon said.
After a first round of preliminary talks in New York last month, North Korea has held back from agreeing to negotiations, which would include China, the United States and South Korea.
The talks are to work out a permanent peace treaty to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-1953 Korean War.
